text.p: The main stories in the Austrian press this Friday are:
DER STANDARD
- The Austrian post service will be split up and the telecoms section separated from Yellow Post and the bus service and floated on the stock market before summer 1998.
- The National Bank is to pay 90 percent of its profits to the state coffers in future.
- Austrian tourism is experiencing it's worst summer ever.
- Unilever is to close its Austrian ice-cream company Eskimo in March 1998, causing the loss of 248 jobs.
- Banks are now advising on new safety measures for sports products manufacturer HTM. Insolvency or liquidation of the company is not an issue.
- Austrian exports to Switzerland rose by just 1.5 percent in the first half of the year to around two billion francs (17 billion schillings).
- There will be no sale of the Bayern-Hypo unit Salzburger Kredit-und Wechsel-Bank (SKWB), said Bayern-Hypo board member Martin Koelsch.
- Half year results of fireproof materials maker Radex-Heraklith (RHI) saw a six perent pretax profit rise to 220 million shillings.
DIE PRESSE
- Hot political intrigue over the division of the Post. Economy Minister Hannes Farnleitner says just the telecoms section should be floated on the stock-exchange.
- Austrian tourism has achieved plumbed new depths with the number of overnight stays down steeply thanks to poor weather.
- The Greens have a new party programme aimed at finding a new way between traditional social politics and neo-liberalism.
KURIER
- Conservative People's Party Economy Minister Hannes Farnleitner is worried about the social partners and the budget.
- A 32 year old Tyrolean killed his four children and ex-wife but failed in his suicide attempt.
- Vienna's Schoenbrunn Zoo celebrates its 245th birthday. Six years ago the zoo was threatened with closure, now it has plans to become the most modern zoo in the world.
- Post & Telecom Austria finance chief Johannes Ditz is fighting to carry through his social plan for PTA employees.
- Austria's third GSM mobile phone license will be up for auction next Friday.
- Austria's leading cement firm Perlmooser AG will leave the Vienna stock-market when French parent company Lafarge offers its small shareholders a pay-off on August 14.
- Building unions fear economic catastrophe in 1998, with housing construction potentially facing a decline of 30 percent.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN

- New salaries for President Thomas Klestil and Chancellor Viktor Klima come into effect today. Klima gets an extra 800,000 schillings gross, but Klestil's pocket becomes two million schillings lighter.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- The Wiener Central Wechsel-und Creditbank (CW-Bank) is looking for a new owner. The bank currently belongs to the Hungarian issuing bank.
WIENER ZEITUNG

- Pension reforms are considered to be in the right direction by 54 percent of Austrians, according to Social Democrat official Andreas Rudas. Apparently only 36 percent of people consider the planned reforms excessive.
- Austrians favour building societies for keeping money, according to a new poll by the Linz research institute Spectra.
